entry.title: Shor's algorithm on cat qubits: estimated resources to factor RSA-2048
entry.summary: Shor's algorithm compiled on cat qubits: 22 593 qubits for RSA-2048 in 3.14 days IACR ePrint · Oct 28, 2026 This paper presents an end-to-end resource estimate of Shor's algorithm on superconducting cat qubits, covering RSA, ECDLP and FFDLP. It compiles the main subroutines to physical-qubit operations on repetition-cat-code and LDPC-cat-code architectures and proposes chip layouts and schedules. Under stated assumptions, factoring RSA-2048 is estimated to require about 23,000 cat qubits and 3.14 days, while solving ECDLP on secp256k1 needs at most 30,000 cat qubits and 1 hour. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present an end-to-end resource estimate of Shor's algorithm on cat qubits, giving chip layouts for RSA-2048, ECDLP and FFDLP and a new parity-Cnot gate.

entry.title: Barriers to Identity-Based Encryption in Generic Group-Action Models
entry.summary: Barriers to Identity-Based Encryption in Generic Group-Action Models IACR ePrint · Oct 28, 2026 This paper studies whether identity-based encryption (IBE) can be built from the basic interface of generic cryptographic group actions. In the type-safe generic group-action model, the authors prove that an IBE scheme whose public parameters contain n non-origin action-set element-handles can support at most n identities, and they show a matching construction that makes this bound tight. The result is extended to random-representation models and to actions with an inversion-like twist, suggesting IBE may require extra algebraic structure or non-black-box techniques. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first tight lower bounds for IBE in generic group-action models, bounding identities by public parameter size with a matching construction.

entry.title: Private information retrieval analyzed through probabilistic inference
entry.summary: PIR through the Lens of Probabilistic Inference IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026 Private Information Retrieval (PIR) lets a client fetch a database entry without servers learning which index was requested. The paper shows that each server's computation in classic PIR protocols amounts to computing a marginal probability of a product distribution, so efficient exact inference algorithms yield faster server computation. It gives improved server algorithms for several structured function classes and, under the randomized Circuit Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis, proves that substantially sublinear server computation cannot be achieved uniformly for all polynomial-size Boolean circuits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link PIR server computation to marginal probability inference, reporting improvements for structured function classes and conditional lower bounds.

entry.title: Faster complete formulas and their application to curves with efficient endomorphisms
entry.summary: Faster complete formulas and their application to curves with efficient endomorphisms IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026 The paper revisits scalar multiplication on prime curves y² = x³ + b with p ≡ 1 (mod 3), a family that includes secp256k1, BN, and BLS curves. It applies a 15-year-old technique in a new way to reduce the best complete addition from 12 to 11 multiplications. Implemented in libsecp256k1, this yields a 5.2% improvement in constant-time fixed-base scalar multiplication. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply a 15-year-old technique to cut complete addition to 11 multiplications and propose a complete tripling formula with exception-free τ-NAF; reported on secp256k1 and BLS curves.

entry.title: An algebraic data structure for fast polynomial evaluation over large-characteristic fields
entry.summary: An Algebraic Polynomial Evaluation Datastructure for Fields of Large Characteristic IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026 This paper studies data structures that evaluate a multivariate polynomial at any input point by using random access to a precomputed encoding of the polynomial. The authors construct algebraic curves over prime fields by using the base-β representation of prime field elements, reducing evaluation recursively to points in boxes of decreasing size. The resulting structure greatly improves the dependence of query complexity on the characteristic p and removes p from the data structure size. The variant of the results is enough to disprove Miltersen's conjecture for all finite fields. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose base-β curve constructions improving query complexity's p-dependence from p^O(1) to d^{O(log log p)}, plus a matching-exponent lower bound.

entry.title: Radical isogeny computation on curves in many models
entry.summary: Radical isogenies on every model IACR ePrint · Oct 28, 2026 This paper studies radical isogeny formulae, which compute a cyclic chain of N-isogenies using one N-th root per step without sampling torsion points. Previously, such formulae for general N were known only in Tate normal form. The authors give radical steps of odd degree N on many curve models, including Montgomery and twisted Edwards curves, and report exact operation counts for each model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend radical isogeny formulas from Tate normal form to many curve models, giving explicit steps for each odd degree with exact operation counts and reported costs.

entry.title: Recovering Falcon Private Keys by Combining Sampler Side-Channel Leakages
entry.summary: Falcon Key Recovery from Joint Sampler Leakages IACR ePrint · Oct 27, 2026 Falcon and the FN-DSA standard based on it create signatures using discrete Gaussian sampling, and power consumption during this step leaks information about secret-dependent values. The paper presents a key-recovery method that combines three observations from each sampler call and turns the resulting candidate sets into constraints on the secret key, solved by regression and integer reconstruction without lattice reduction like LLL or BKZ. The attack recovers all 50 evaluation keys on PQClean Falcon-512 and still recovers 38 of 50 keys on c-fn-dsa, showing that instruction-level normalization alone is insufficient. ★★★★★ Notable: Fuses three sampler side-channel observations to recover Falcon keys without LLL/BKZ; the abstract reports recovering all 50 evaluation keys on Cortex-M4 with a median of 11 signatures.

entry.title: Quantum key distribution secured by a bound on information leakage
entry.summary: Prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution from a bound on information leakage arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper examines whether, in prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution, a single bound on information leakage from the sender's source can replace a detailed model of the source. The authors show that this bound, quantified by the probability of guessing the input from everything the source emits, suffices to prove security against collective attacks, with no assumptions on the form, dimension, energy or purity of the emitted states. They note that the standard B92 and BB84 protocols cannot certify a key under this assumption, whereas closely related protocols can reach one secret bit per round in the ideal limit. For noisy implementations, key rates are computed with semidefinite programming relaxations, and the best protocols tolerate visibilities down to 0.84, corresponding to an 8% quantum bit error rate, versus the 11% threshold of device-dependent BB84. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes security proofs from only a sender-side leakage bound, without modeling the source; the authors report one key bit per round ideally and tolerance down to visibility 0.84.

entry.title: SecDMP: A Provably Secure Data Prefetcher Defense (Extended Version)
entry.summary: SecDMP: Provably Secure Data Memory-Dependent Prefetching (Extended Version) arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 Data memory-dependent prefetchers (DMPs) are a CPU optimization in recent mainstream processors that can improve performance but may leak secrets through side channels. The paper classifies DMP leakage, categorizes existing and new attacks, and validates the analysis by implementing open-source DMPs on a RISC-V processor. It proposes SecDMP, a hardware defense in which secrets are marked in memory so DMPs never encode them in the microarchitecture. The authors formally prove SecDMP adds no leakage beyond a baseline without DMPs. ★★★★★ Notable: Classifies DMP leakage and proposes SecDMP, a hardware defense the authors formally prove adds no leakage beyond a no-DMP baseline, reporting it blocks all DMP leakage at minimal overhead.

entry.title: FeatureArc: Testing Coding Agents on Features That Grow Over Time
entry.summary: FeatureArc: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Evolving Features arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper introduces FeatureArc, a benchmark that evaluates coding agents on software features that evolve through successive stages, with each extension building on the agent's own earlier code. Tasks are built from repository histories and checked with executable tests across four programming languages. Evaluating 10 agents on 73 tasks, pooled success falls from 62.7% at the first stage to 28.5% on the whole feature. Inherited defects from earlier stages are a common cause of failure. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose FeatureArc, a benchmark and pipeline for evolving features; across 10 agents and 73 tasks, pooled success falls from 62.7% at the first stage to 28.5% for the whole feature.

entry.title: Do Generalist Skill Optimizers Really Help AI Agents? A Bipartite Attribution Rethink
entry.summary: Does Your Generalist Skill Optimizer Really Incentivize Agentic Tasks? Rethinking Skill Optimization via Bipartite Attribution arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper introduces BiPA, a method for evaluating skill optimizers that rewrite an AI agent's natural-language procedures to improve performance on long-horizon tasks. Across three optimizers, three benchmarks, and two models, learned skills succeed about as often as their hand-written seeds, and development-set gains vanish on the test set. The optimized skills also increase input tokens by about 16%, largely because the added rules cause extra conversation turns. The authors propose four principles, including accepting only edits whose gains exceed what selection alone would report. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes BiPA, using a selection baseline and bipartite attribution: learned skills match their seed's success, dev gains vanish on test, and input tokens rise about 16%.

They also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors with improved seed and output lengths. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show matrix samplers and quantum-proof extractors are equivalent, and use this to build explicit strong matrix samplers with fewer samples and shorter seeds than prior work.

entry.title: Blindfold: Keeping Random Audit Checks Hidden from LLM Agents
entry.summary: Blindfold: Keeping the Audit Coin Secret from LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies audit-based certification, which limits an LLM agent's violation rate by auditing a random fraction of its actions and reweighting the results. The authors show that validity also requires the audit coin to stay hidden from the agent before its action is committed. They define this as pre-commit noninterference, measure it, and derive bounds on the resulting bias. Experiments on a monitor and a real LLM agent show that a visible audit notice leaks the coin and breaks the certificate, while a silent audit or a fresh coin per audited call restores validity. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes pre-commit noninterference and characterizes the bias and leakage precisely; shows the audit coin can leak to agents via timing, and reports that a real LLM agent breaks the plain certificate

entry.title: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Scaling Embeddings in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Embedding Scaling in Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper introduces V-LUMEN, a visual lookup memory for vision-language models that adds external memory instead of increasing model size. It discretizes visual features with a frozen codebook, builds spatially aware memory keys by hashing, modulates them with text-conditioned relevance signals, and fuses retrieved embeddings into the backbone through a gated residual pathway. On five reasoning-intensive benchmarks it improves a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone and transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks whose images are disjoint from the training data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors bring lookup-based external memory to VLMs, using spatial hashing and gated residual fusion; the abstract reports gains on five reasoning benchmarks for a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B and zero-shot

It finds that many languages appear in only one benchmark, low-resource languages are evaluated on far fewer task categories, and 56% of dataset-language instances are translated from English. entry.title: PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search
entry.summary: PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents PailitaoMMSearch, a system that generates product Semantic IDs directly from a raw query image and free-form instruction, aiming for unified end-to-end multimodal search. It scales along data, intent, and scenario dimensions, using continual pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. The system is deployed in Taobao Pailitao, and a controlled online A/B test reports statistically significant gains in item page views, transactions, and gross merchandise value. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes PailitaoMMSearch, a unified end-to-end multimodal system generating product Semantic IDs from query images and instructions; the authors report Taobao A/B gains of +17.90% page views, +27.04%

entry.title: DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding
entry.summary: DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper introduces DocXEval, a comprehensive explainability framework for multimodal document understanding that combines text, layout, and image. It adapts existing explainable AI methods and metrics to this setting and adds multi-target variants for tasks such as semantic entity recognition. The authors evaluate 13 XAI methods across 3 tasks, 8 datasets, 4 models, and 17 metrics, finding that Occlusion is the most faithful and interpretable overall. The work also includes a meta-evaluation of metrics and dataset-wide analyses of model behavior. ★★★★ Notable: First XAI framework for multimodal document understanding, systematically evaluating 13 methods and 17 metrics across 8 datasets and 4 models; the authors report Occlusion as most faithful overall.

entry.title: Can Lightweight Decision Models Classify Why Retrieved Sources Conflict in RAG?
entry.summary: Do We Need an LLM to Know Why Sources Conflict? Decision Models for Knowledge-Conflict Typing in RAG arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 When retrieved sources disagree, the appropriate response depends on the type of conflict. This paper tests whether decision models, which output probabilities over fixed options in a single forward pass, can classify conflict types quickly and cheaply. On the CONFLICTS benchmark, 10 of 11 decision models match or exceed Gemini 2.5 Flash (61.3%) in accuracy, at 4 to 39 times lower billed cost. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply decision models to RAG knowledge-conflict typing on CONFLICTS, comparing them with Gemini models and cascades; they report most match or beat Gemini 2.5 Flash accuracy at lower cost

entry.title: GUI-JEPA: A Fast, Decoder-Free Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents Using JEPA Latents
entry.summary: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper introduces GUI-JEPA, a decoder-free action policy for mobile GUI agents built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture. It selects actions in the latent space of an encoder pretrained on unlabelled GUI screenshots, using an action- and region-conditioned predictor to score all candidate actions in one batched pass. entry.title: Evolving Agent Teams: A Multi-Agent Framework Escaping Local Optima
entry.summary: Evolving Agent Teams arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper finds that existing coding agents converge to local optima when optimizing real-world expert-written GPU kernels such as FlashInfer. The authors propose Evolving Agent Teams, in which a central supervisor diagnoses local optima and restructures the agent team, while a persistent file system stores accumulated experience. With an extended token budget, the generated CUDA kernel reaches a 1.2x mean speedup over the production FlashInfer MLA paged decode kernel and wins on 36 of 47 FlashInfer-Bench workloads. ★★★★ Notable: A central supervisor diagnoses local optima and restructures agent teams, using a persistent file system to accumulate experience; the authors report speedups on real FlashInfer kernel and other tasks

entry.title: Right Click, Wrong Box: Judging GUI Clicks by Their Outcomes
entry.summary: Right Click, Wrong Box: Grading GUI Grounding by What a Click Does arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper argues that GUI grounding benchmarks count a click as correct only inside one annotated box, even though interfaces often expose the same action through several elements. The authors define a click as correct when it produces the same outcome as the annotated target, and build outcome maps and an execution judge by executing about a thousand clicks per page on live web applications. Testing three strong grounders on a code forge and an online shop, they find that many box-rejected clicks still reach the intended outcome, and an audit on ScreenSpot-v2 yields corrections of 0.2 to 1.8 points. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors grade GUI clicks by outcome rather than annotated box, reporting that roughly one in five to one in three box-rejected clicks reach the intended result, a shift comparable to reported mode

entry.title: HqcLethe: streaming HQC key encapsulation for tiny stateless servers
entry.summary: HqcLethe: Streaming HQC Encapsulation for Tiny Stateless Servers arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents HqcLethe, a stateless post-quantum key exchange that streams an HQC key encapsulation in packet-sized pieces, so servers need not buffer multi-packet handshakes and avoid memory-exhaustion attacks. It uses the Chinese remainder theorem to split polynomial multiplication into independent, masked remainders, one per packet. The authors prove in Rocq with SSProve that the masked pieces reveal no more than an ordinary HQC ciphertext, and verify session secrecy, server authentication and forward secrecy in ProVerif. entry.title: Language Models Keep Abandoned Analyses: Residue and Adaptation after Garden-Path Sentences
entry.summary: Language Models Keep Abandoned Analyses: Residue and Adaptation after Garden-Path Sentences arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper examines whether language models keep using syntactic analyses they have abandoned after reading garden-path sentences. Across 24 open models, the authors find a residue of the abandoned analysis that raises later object attachment, plus an adaptation toward the resolved structure. Activation patching shows the residue is carried by noun-phrase states computed before disambiguation, and replacing them removes most of it in the larger models. ★★★★ Notable: Activation patching separates residue from adaptation after garden-path sentences across 24 open models, also testing persistence of overridden statements and transfer to the human paradigm.

entry.title: Does LLM pre-training usually happen at the edge of stability?
entry.summary: Does LLM Pre-Training Typically Occur at the Edge of Stability? arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper revisits how well quadratic approximations model neural network training, especially in large language model (LLM) pretraining. It identifies an "Edge of Convexity" (EoC) failure mode, where persistent negative curvature makes the quadratic dynamics diverge regardless of learning rate, and proposes a generalized Edge of Stability (EoS) definition for stochastic adaptive optimizers. Across LLM pretraining runs with models up to 787M parameters, EoC is always observed, while EoS is common but not universal, disappearing at sufficiently small learning rates or batch sizes below a critical threshold. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a learning-rate-independent Edge of Convexity and generalizes Edge of Stability to stochastic training with adaptive optimizers; the authors report EoC consistently appears and EoS is common

entry.title: Learning to correct interpolation for reconstructing intermediate scientific fields
entry.summary: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper proposes iFLEX, a method for reconstructing unobserved intermediate scientific fields between two observation times. It first forms a time-weighted average of the two observations, then uses a conditional diffusion model to learn and generate the residual between this average and the true intermediate field. The authors evaluate it on Navier-Stokes Kraichnan turbulence, Shanghai radar precipitation, and sea surface temperature data, reporting lower reconstruction error than the compared baselines. ★★★★ Notable: Over weighted averaging, a conditional diffusion model learns the residual; the authors report lower reconstruction error than optical-flow and video diffusion baselines on three scientific datasets.

entry.summary: Nonlinear Direct Feedback Alignment for Scalable Backpropagation-Free Training arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper addresses the biological implausibility and backward locking of backpropagation by improving Direct Feedback Alignment (DFA). entry.summary: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 Diffusion vision-language models process the full input at every denoising step, and visual tokens make up 89-97% of that input on the studied benchmarks. entry.title: Shows that all bidders in repeated auctions cannot jointly achieve no-regret learning under budget constraints.
entry.summary: Impossibility of No-Regret in Multi-Agent Bidding arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies repeated second-price auctions with multiple pacing bidders facing budget or return-on-investment constraints. It proves that it is computationally impossible for all bidders to achieve no-regret simultaneously, linking high variance in bidding systems to high regret. The authors show joint no-regret is PPAD-hard by extracting a pacing equilibrium from low-variance systems. Simulations suggest that several widely used bidding algorithms can cycle and display high-variance behavior even in simple markets. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show joint no-regret for multiple budget-constrained bidders is computationally impossible (PPAD-hard) via a variance-regret link, and report cycling high-variance behavior in simulations

entry.title: Tight limits on fair AMM mechanism design under weak efficiency
entry.summary: Tight Characterizations of AMM Mechanism Design under Weak Efficiency arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies miner extractable value (MEV) in automated market makers (AMMs), where block builders can profit by controlling transaction order. It proves that no deterministic, anonymous batch AMM can be both incentive compatible and weakly locally efficient under plain consensus without fair sequencing, even with censorship resilience and unlimited block space. The impossibility relies on Sybil identities, over-reporting budgets, and misreporting values. Removing any one of these strategic capabilities makes both properties achievable under censorship resilience. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove deterministic anonymous batch AMMs cannot satisfy both IC and wLE under plain consensus; removing any one of three strategic capabilities restores feasibility.

entry.summary: Sybil-Proofness of Generalized Adaptive Clinching and Implications for Blockchain Mechanism Design arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper examines whether the adaptive clinching auction for budget-constrained bidders stays robust when a bidder splits its budget across fake identities. The authors propose a generalized adaptive clinching framework and prove that bidders gain nothing by splitting into any number of identities, as long as their total reported budget does not exceed their enforceable true budget. entry.title: Noise Shapes the Surplus: Strategic Play Against No-Regret Learners
entry.summary: Noise Shapes the Surplus: Strategic Play Against No-Regret Learners arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how an optimizer in zero-sum games can gain cumulative payoff above the minimax benchmark against no-regret learners, here Follow-the-Regularized-Leader algorithms, that act on noisy payoff scores with decaying learning rates. Passive play earns at most constant surplus, while a clairvoyant optimizer secures surplus scaling with the inverse learning rate when the mean response is profitable. Active alternating play can still extract surplus from the learner's movement when it is not, and at the canonical rate the noiseless Ω(√T) surplus is recovered under mean-zero, finite-variance perturbations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that in zero-sum games, optimizers can still extract strategic surplus from noisy FTRL learners with decaying rates, including Ω(1/η_T) and Ω(∑η_t) results and an Ω(√T) rate at η_t∝

entry.title: PRISM: A benchmark testing how reliable pathology AI models are when labels are scarce.

entry.title: Can AI scientists tell what is truly new?
entry.summary: Do AI Scientists Know What's New? arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper examines how AI scientific discovery pipelines can determine whether a generated research idea is meaningfully novel. The authors build an evaluation framework with temporal ground truth, using four datasets of 1,060 proposals drawn from published papers, reviewer disputes, and ideas later realized by researchers. entry.title: Learning-Augmented Coordination Mechanisms: Using Demand Predictions to Improve Equilibrium Efficiency in Congestion Games
entry.summary: Learning-Augmented Coordination Mechanisms arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how selfish behavior reduces efficiency in decentralized resource allocation. It proposes learning-augmented coordination mechanisms that use a possibly inaccurate demand prediction to modify resource costs, with a confidence parameter β that yields near-optimal performance when predictions are accurate while keeping a good worst-case equilibrium guarantee. The paper also gives robustness bounds and impossibility results, including limits on error tolerance in non-atomic games. ★★★★ Notable: Introduces learning-augmented coordination mechanisms for congestion games, aiming for near-optimal performance under accurate predictions while retaining PoS guarantees, with impossibility results.

entry.summary: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents SO-101 Bench, a simulated benchmark for language-instructed spatial manipulation on the low-cost SO-101 robot arm, built on an Isaac Lab digital twin of a real setup. It includes four tasks, 138 objects, 916 evaluation episodes, and 3,629 simulated demonstrations. Policy rankings in simulation match those on the physical robot, though simulation overestimates success rates. entry.summary: kw-bench: Breaking Frontier Harnesses on Real-World Tasks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper introduces kw-bench, a benchmark built from real audit, tax and similar engagements described by specialists. entry.summary: SOMA: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Egocentric Behavior and Body-Motion Understanding arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper introduces SOMA, a benchmark of 1,632 human-verified questions for understanding body motion from egocentric video, covering body configuration, motion dynamics, and temporal reasoning. entry.title: HELICS: Generating Synthetic Genomes at Biobank Scale with Latent Flow Matching
entry.summary: HELICS: Biobank-scale Conditional Synthetic Genome Generation via Latent Flow Matching arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents HELICS, a framework for generating synthetic genome-wide SNP-level genotype data from biobank-scale datasets without requiring haplotype phasing. entry.summary: A Smart Instant Book Filter Model based on Dual-Objective Optimization arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper proposes a smart instant book filter system for hospitality marketplaces, deciding which listings in search results receive instant booking. The system aims to increase the instant book rate while keeping the overall booking rate from decreasing, a dual-objective optimization problem. A/B tests with global users show it outperforms previous human-expert-tuned models on both instant book rate and overall booking rate. The system has been deployed to production and serves millions of users daily. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a smart instant book filter maximizing instant book rate under a no-drop booking-rate constraint; the authors report global A/B tests beating expert-tuned models, deployed to millions.

entry.summary: The Complexity of Strategizing Against No-Regret Learners: Pure When It Is Easy, Hard Even When Mixed arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies how hard it is to optimize a strategy against a known online learner in repeated finite-horizon games. entry.title: Algorithm guaranteeing baseline protection and robust performance across adversarial and stochastic settings
entry.summary: Three Worlds for the Price of a Logarithm: Baseline-Protected Best-of-Both-Worlds Combinatorial Semi-Bandits arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper proposes DUET, a horizon-free phased mixing algorithm for combinatorial semi-bandits with arbitrary finite action sets. Two observable tests decide when to double the learning weight and when to double the empirical-regret budget and restart. Assuming the baseline selects every arm with positive probability, expected regret relative to the baseline stays logarithmic in T. Regret to any fixed action is Õ(√T) under non-anticipating adversarial losses and polylogarithmic and gap-dependent under i.i.d. losses with a unique optimal action. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose DUET, a horizon-free phased mixing scheme for combinatorial semi-bandits, reporting baseline protection, adversarial and stochastic regret bounds at the cost of a logarithm.

entry.title: Explicit Reed-Solomon codes with optimal list and line decoding
entry.summary: Explicit Reed-Solomon Subspace Designs: Optimal List and Line Decoding arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper constructs explicit Reed-Solomon codes over extension fields that can be list-decoded from a fraction 1-R-ε of errors with optimal list size O((1-R)/ε). A simpler strongly explicit evaluation-point construction achieves list size (1/ε)^O(1/ε). Both constructions admit deterministic list-decoding algorithms running in polynomial time. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give explicit Reed-Solomon codes with near-optimal constant list size via subspace designs, and report a new reduction yielding line decoding and proximity results.

entry.title: count-catcher: Turning model counting certificates into Lean theorems
entry.summary: count-catcher: Lean Theorems from Model Counting Certificates arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper presents count-catcher, a tool that converts a CPOG certificate from the exact model counter d4 into a Lean theorem stating that a CNF formula has exactly N models over V variables. With an encoding lemma, this becomes a theorem about the number of combinatorial objects. The authors combine these results with Mathlib and prove the number of Latin squares of order 8 as a weighted sum of hundreds of certified counts drawn from about eight terabytes of certificates. ★★★★ Notable: Turns model counting certificates into Lean theorems; the authors prove the number of order-8 Latin squares and report that CPOG's unverified checker gave wrong counts.

entry.title: Don't Pick a Winner: Knowledge Conflicts Need a Prior, Not a Rule. A study on how retrieval-augmented language models should resolve conflicts between retrieved context and their own knowledge.
entry.summary: Don't Pick a Winner: Knowledge Conflicts Need a Prior, Not a Rule arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies how retrieval-augmented language models should answer when retrieved context and the model's own knowledge disagree. It argues that fixed design-time rules are wrong in some settings and that resolving conflicts requires separate evidence from each source and a prior on how often the context is right. On the GRACE benchmark and ClashEval, the authors' method, which voices knowledge notes with calibrated confidence and commits or abstains under a prior, outperforms baselines. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes resolving retrieval-context versus parametric-knowledge conflicts with a prior rather than a fixed rule, built as a two-source selector with exact prior shift; the authors report overall GRAC

entry.summary: They Will See Johnny's Message: A Measurement Study of Post-Quantum Cryptography Across Email Delivery Paths arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper systematically measures post-quantum cryptography (PQC) deployment across email delivery stages, including relay, submission, and access services, as well as sending servers and OpenPGP and S/MIME implementations. entry.title: Symmetry breaking under limited model capacity: a paper on why optimal models lose rotational symmetry
entry.summary: Symmetry Breaking Is the Price of Finite Capacity arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies why the best model for a rotation-symmetric problem can break that symmetry when capacity is limited. For a Gaussian problem with a bilinear predictor, it derives an exact log-loss price of symmetry and extends the result to attention heads fitted to symmetric similarities. It reports that with peaked softmax attention, broken heads beat every whole-shell symmetric head at 16 of 20 head dimensions. ★★★★ Notable: Derives an exact log-loss price for symmetry under limited capacity and tests predicted symmetry-breaking dimensions and rotation sensitivity in attention heads. entry.title: Log-To-Leak: Prompt injection attacks on tool-using LLM agents via the Model Context Protocol
entry.summary: Log-To-Leak: Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents via the Model Context Protocol arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies security risks for LLM agents that access external tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It introduces Log-To-Leak, an attack that makes an agent place an extra, attacker-controlled tool call after the legitimate one, leaking the user query, server name, server response, and agent response. Across 18 valid model-server pairs, the attack reaches an attack success rate of 62.64% to 100%, and three tested defenses still leave over 55% residual success on GitHub MCP with GPT-4o. entry.title: Minimax-optimal small-loss bounds for online linear optimisation on ℓp balls
entry.summary: Minimax-Optimal Small-Loss Bounds for Online Linear Optimisation on ℓ_p Balls arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies full-information online linear optimisation over the unit ℓp ball for fixed p between 2 and infinity. It presents a follow-the-regularised-leader algorithm whose regret depends on the cumulative excess loss and the dimension, and shows this rate is minimax-optimal for each fixed p. It also analyses a switching extension that keeps the sharp constant, and computes the exact log T coefficient of expected regret for i.i.d. losses. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a small-loss regret bound for online linear optimisation on ℓp balls, reporting that it matches minimax lower bounds with a constant optimal as p→∞, and analyse paths where FTL fails.

entry.title: Closed-loop planning that scores candidate speeds without imitation, for end-to-end autonomous driving
entry.summary: Closed-Loop Aware Planning via Imitation-Free Speed Scoring for End-to-End Autonomous Driving arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper proposes CLAP-AD, a planning head that plugs into existing end-to-end driving models. It learns the path through imitation but scores candidate speeds with a learned function supervised by physically grounded safety constraints, allowing explicit speed control at test time. On Bench2Drive-Speed it reaches a Speed-Adherence Score of 82.53, 12.9 points above the previous best baseline TFv6, while keeping strong closed-loop driving performance. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes CLAP-AD, a plug-in planning head that scores candidate speeds without imitation, enabling test-time speed control without speed-conditioned training. entry.title: Counting the Bandages: a paper on measuring the time AI saves
entry.summary: Counting the Bandages: On measuring the time that AI saves arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 This paper examines what it means for AI assistance to save time, arguing that time saved should be read alongside the errors the work lets through rather than taken from a stopwatch alone. It defines model-free measures of time saved and excess escaped defects, and re-analyzes public data from METR's developer study and published GDPval results. A small pre-specified experiment then tests how AI reviewers change their checking when told the drafter's error rate is higher or lower than it actually is. ★★★★ Notable: The authors argue time saved by AI should be read alongside the errors it lets through, proposing model-free quantities for time saved and excess escaped defects plus a break-even defect cost. entry.summary: Reverse Substitution in Secret Sharing: The Critical One-Half Threshold and a Route to Superpolynomial Lower Bounds IACR ePrint · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies substitution, a way of building composite access structures by replacing one participant of an outer structure with an inner structure in secret sharing. It asks whether the contribution vector of any scheme for the composite structure can be reverse-factored into vectors for the outer and inner factors. The authors show exact reversal fails via a counterexample with factor 8/9, but prove a factor of 1/2 is always attainable. entry.title: CTGREP: Finding Compiler-Induced Timing Leaks in Crypto Code at Scale
entry.summary: Analyzing Compiler-induced Constant-time Violations with Compiler at Scale IACR ePrint · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents CTGREP, a compiler-based framework that uses differential analysis across the whole compilation chain to find where compilers break constant-time cryptographic code, how the violation is introduced, and which configurations cause it. The authors applied it to seven complete cryptographic libraries across three Clang versions, six platforms, and thousands of compiler configurations. entry.title: Hidden in the Comments: Context-Injection Attacks on Code LLMs
entry.summary: Hidden in the Comments: A Context-Injection Attack Surface in Code LLMs arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper examines whether insecure instructions hidden in code comments and other development context can push code-generating language models toward vulnerable code. The authors tested ten open-weight models across ten web-application weakness classes and found that embedded malicious instructions produced far more vulnerable outputs than benign prompts. They conclude that inference-time context injection is a substantial attack surface and suggest provenance-aware training objectives as a response. ★★★★ Notable: Shows inference-time comment injection drives code LLMs to vulnerable outputs; novel attack surface, with broad experiments across ten models and weakness classes.

entry.title: Evidence Found but Not Read: How Extracted Text Bridges the Retrieval-Reading Gap in Document VLMs
entry.summary: Found but Not Read: When Extracted Text Closes the Retrieval-Reading Gap in Document Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper examines retrieval-augmented document question answering, where a vision-language model may fail to use evidence even after the correct page is retrieved. Using a paired protocol on FoveDoc-Bench, the authors compare answers from page images alone with answers from the same images plus extracted text. entry.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Whether LLMs Behave Differently When Tested in Indic Languages
entry.summary: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages? arXiv · Oct 16, 2026 This paper studies whether large language models can tell they are being tested, a behavior called evaluation awareness, and checks whether it also appears in five Indic languages alongside English. Four instruction-tuned models from three families were tested with cues saying they are monitored or under a safety test. When told they were being tested, models refused harmful requests more often, in all models and languages. entry.title: Likelihood Is Not Authorship: Measuring Human Contribution in AI-Assisted Writing
entry.summary: Likelihood Is Not Authorship: Can We Reliably Measure Human Contribution in AI-Assisted Writing? arXiv · Oct 14, 2026 The paper shows that a common method of estimating human contribution to AI-assisted text, based on how well a person's prompt predicts the final text, can be easily manipulated. They report this effect across news and scientific abstracts and LLMs ranging from 3.8B to 753B parameters. entry.title: Optimal Test for Distribution Support Size
entry.summary: Optimal Support Size Testing arXiv · Oct 14, 2026 The paper presents an optimal tester that decides whether an unknown probability distribution is supported on n elements or is ε-far from such a distribution in total variation distance. Its sample complexity is Θ(n/(ε log n)), improving on the earlier O(n/(ε log n) · log(min{1/ε, n})) bound of Ferreira Pinto Jr. and Harms (STOC 2025). The authors also provide a fairly good lower bound on support size. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present an optimal support-size tester with sample complexity Θ(n/(ε log n)), improving the prior logarithmic factor, and also give a lower bound on support size.

entry.title: Draft-KV: Learning Useful Latent Communication Between Language Models
entry.summary: Draft-KV: Learning Useful Latent Communication Between Language Models arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies language models passing internal states to each other instead of decoded text, and shows that higher receiver accuracy alone does not prove the receiver used the message content. The proposed Draft-KV method sends the key-value states formed while the sharer drafts an answer, with both models kept frozen and only 1.05M interface parameters trained. With a Qwen3-8B sharer, a frozen Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct receiver reaches 78.04% on MMLU-Redux, up from 37.45% alone. The authors report that the communication also transfers to held-out tasks. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes draft KV-state latent communication between LMs, testing content use with mismatched messages; reports 78.04% on MMLU-Redux versus 36.40% with reassigned messages.

entry.summary: Copying Before Suppression: What Drives a Below-Chance Dip During Language Model Training? arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper studies a temporary dip below chance in an Indirect Object Identification task during early language model training, when models prefer the repeated name over the correct one. entry.summary: PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper addresses the risk that tool-using large language model agents can be steered by poisoned tool metadata, retrieved pages, memory, or reusable skills, since vetting artifacts before admission does not fully solve the problem. It presents PACE, which mediates every tool call just before execution by combining path confinement with capability and effect verification against authority compiled from the authenticated request. entry.title: Learning to cover locally: neural optimization when each node sees only nearby information.
entry.summary: Learning to Cover Locally: Graph Neural Combinatorial Optimization under a Hard Information Horizon arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The paper studies combinatorial optimization where each node sees only its k-hop neighborhood yet must contribute to a globally feasible solution, formalized as local set cover. entry.title: Universal Inductive Inference of Quantum States: a framework for learning and predicting quantum sources from measurement data
entry.summary: Universal Inductive Inference of Quantum States arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper extends Solomonoff's universal inductive inference to quantum systems, introducing a framework for learning and predicting quantum sources that may have arbitrary correlations and entanglement across time. Given past measurement outcomes and post-measurement systems, the learner outputs a joint state predicting the next outcome while preserving correlations with past systems. The authors give an information-theoretic inference algorithm with round complexity O(sε⁻²δ⁻¹), prove a matching lower bound in the relevant regime, and construct a non-i.i.d. state tomography algorithm. entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use: Reusable Learned Policies for Repeated Computer Tasks
entry.summary: Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use: Learning Reusable Policies for Reliable and Efficient Execution arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper proposes running recurring computer workflows with learned, executable code policies instead of having an agent re-plan every step. Stable decisions such as ordering and loops are fixed in code, while observation-dependent steps like grounding and state checks are handled by neural models. The policies are learned through neuro-symbolic policy iteration and guarded by a pre-action verifier during deployment. The authors report the highest Pass^3 across four settings on OSWorld-Verified and ScienceBoard, with lower per-run cost and latency. ★★★★ Notable: The authors learn executable neuro-symbolic policies for recurring computer workflows, reporting top Pass^3 on OSWorld-Verified and ScienceBoard with much lower per-run cost and latency.

entry.title: RareDx: Controlled knowledge integration and knowledge-graph-based policy optimization for rare-disease diagnosis
entry.summary: RareDx: Controlled Knowledge Integration and Graph-Grounded Policy Optimization for Rare-Disease Diagnosis arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents RareDx, a system for rare-disease diagnosis, a long-tail reasoning problem where language models often favor common conditions. entry.title: Certified automation of LLM agent evaluation: letting an automatic judge score part of agent trajectories with a guaranteed error rate
entry.summary: Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper asks what share of LLM agent evaluation an automatic judge can take over while keeping the error rate among auto-decided trajectories below a set budget. It introduces a task-level bootstrap certificate that stays valid where naive certificates overstate safety. A 4B judge certifies 0.30 to 0.59 of evaluation on tool-use and web corpora at alpha=0.1. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a task-level bootstrap certificate for selective automatic judging of LLM agent trajectories, bounding error and doubling as a self-training filter.

entry.title: Fooling Many Frontier MLLMs with One Black-Box Adversarial Attack
entry.summary: One Attack to Fool Them All: Highly Transferable Black-Box Adversarial Attacks on Frontier MLLMs arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper investigates whether a single adversarial image can consistently mislead diverse frontier multimodal large language models in black-box settings. The authors propose O-Attack, which exploits a broad, cross-modally aligned semantic space in surrogate models and optimizes perturbations through semantic consensus. The reported attack success rates on GPT-5.4, Claude-4.6, and Gemini-3.1 rise from 29.1%, 42.8%, and 38.2% to 77.2%, 81.6%, and 80.9%, and the method outperforms six prior approaches across 24 MLLMs. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes O-Attack, a black-box transfer attack exploiting cross-modally aligned semantic spaces of surrogate models; the abstract reports large success-rate gains on GPT-5.4, Claude-4.6 and Gemini-3.1

entry.summary: Separability rigidity of Gaussian states under positive domination arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper proves that a finite-mode Gaussian state is separable across a fixed mode partition if it dominates a nonzero positive operator that is separable across that partition. entry.title: Quantum Networking at Quantum Computing Speed: Kilohertz Entanglement Between Different Quantum Systems
entry.summary: Quantum Networking at the Speed of Quantum Computation: Kilohertz Entanglement in a Heterogeneous Quantum System arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 The paper entangles a trapped barium ion with a silicon-vacancy center in a diamond nanophotonic cavity. A photon from the ion is converted in wavelength and encoding, reflected off the cavity system, and detected, and one detected photon signals successful entanglement. Including all conversion losses, the average generation rate is 1.03 kHz, about one Bell pair per millisecond, matching the cycle time of planned trapped-ion processors. ★★★★ Notable: Entangles a trapped ion with a diamond SiV center at about 1 kHz, four times faster than prior ion-ion photonic links, shown experimentally.

entry.title: Equivalence of topological indices for U(1)⋊Z₂-symmetric quantum spin chains
entry.summary: The equivalence of topological indices for U(1)rtimesℤ₂-symmetric quantum spin chains arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies symmetry-protected topological phases in integer-spin quantum chains with on-site U(1)⋊Z₂ symmetry. It proves that Ogata's operator-algebraic index and Tasaki's elementary twist index are equivalent, giving an explicit error bound for computing the index. Combined with a boundary-field gap theorem and earlier calculations, it shows that the infinite S=1 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain has a symmetric gapped ground state with both indices equal to −1. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove equivalence of Ogata's and Tasaki's twist indices for U(1)⋊Z2 integer-spin chains with explicit error bound, and report both indices equal -1 for the infinite S=1 Heisenberg chain.

entry.title: Collectivity: a mechanism that limits quantum entanglement even with long-range interactions
entry.summary: Collectivity limits quantum entanglement arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how ground-state quantum entanglement is limited in gapped many-body systems with long-range power-law interactions. The authors show that many weak interactions produce fluctuations controlled by their square-summed strength, a mechanism they call collectivity. They derive logarithmic or subextensive entanglement bounds for arbitrary bipartitions and polylogarithmic bounds for regular bipartitions, and show several of these scalings are optimal. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show collectivity, not locality, limits entanglement under power-law interactions, reporting entanglement bounds and optimality results for long-range many-body systems.

entry.title: Quantum data processing equality: a paper turning the quantum data processing inequality into an exact equality
entry.summary: Quantum data processing equality arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper promotes the quantum data processing inequality, which states that quantum relative entropy does not increase under quantum channels, to an exact equality using boundary and surface Poisson integral representations across a complex strip. The relative-entropy loss splits into two nonnegative components: a Petz recovery term governing state reconstructibility and a boundary term measuring mismatch of relative modular dynamics. The authors also establish recovery bounds at any prescribed modular parameter, with optimal square-root scaling in the relative entropy loss. ★★★★ Notable: Promotes the quantum data processing inequality to an exact equality via Poisson integral representations, decomposing the relative-entropy loss into Petz recovery and boundary terms.

entry.title: DisCoMBO: Distributional-conformance method for expert-guided black-box optimization
entry.summary: DisCoMBO: Steering Expert-in-the-Loop Black-Box Optimization via Distributional Conformance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper addresses how to incorporate expert knowledge into sequential model-based optimization using Probabilistic Circuits as surrogates. entry.summary: Tracekit: Tamper-Evident Intent-Reasoning-Action Auditing for AI Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 AI agents run commands, edit code, send email and move money with operators' credentials, but their logs can usually be altered. entry.summary: Right Facts, Wrong Rule: Scope-Transfer Poisoning of Retrieval-Augmented Generation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies retrieval-augmented generation systems that apply a rule outside the scope where it is valid, so correct facts support a wrong answer. entry.title: ATTUNER: Reusing Agent Context KV States Without Recomputation
entry.summary: ATTUNER: Recomputation-Free Agentic Context KV Reuse arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 LLM agents repeatedly load reusable content such as skills, documents, and memory into their context, and re-encoding it each time wastes computation. The paper proposes ATTUNER, a query-side method that inserts low-rank adapters into a frozen artifact cache and is trained by distilling full-prefill distributions. entry.title: Self-Retrospection Distillation: Using After-the-Fact Experience to Build Advance Foresight
entry.summary: Self-Retrospection Distillation: Turning Post-hoc Experiences into Prior Foresight arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper proposes Self-Retrospection Distillation (SRD), a method that uses information from completed trajectories to train the same policy to make predictions before acting. entry.title: One Leak, Lasting Gains: Binding Keys to Context to Deter Collusion
entry.summary: When One Leak Pays Forever: Context Binding and the Price of Deterring Collusion arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper studies collusion in threshold-encrypted mempools, where a coalition of decryption committee members that sells its decryption capability to a front-runner can expose every later block the capability still decrypts. entry.summary: SlideDP: Scaling Host-Resident LLM Fine-Tuning Across Multiple GPUs arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents SlideDP, a synchronous data-parallel runtime for fine-tuning large language models that exceed GPU memory, using host-resident state on multi-GPU systems. entry.summary: CAST: Cost-Aware Speculative Trees from One-Pass Block Drafters arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Speculative decoding speeds up large language models by cheaply drafting future tokens and verifying them in parallel. entry.summary: ESTHER: Egocentric Stereo Hand Estimation and Reconstruction in the Wild arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents ESTHER, a model that estimates and reconstructs metric 3D hand structure from egocentric stereo cameras worn by a person. The authors also build ESTHER3D, a dataset with model-generated labels for in-the-wild training and motion-capture ground truth for testing. entry.title: Perfect Reconstruction Cannot Reveal If Two VAE Codebooks Agree
entry.summary: Perfect Reconstruction Cannot Show Whether Two Codebooks on a VAE's Latent Space Agree arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Many systems read a variational autoencoder's latent space as discrete codes and assume each latent is decoded as the code it was written as. It builds two VAEs with perfect reconstruction, exact inference, and identical ELBO and code histograms, yet with agreement of 1 and 0. entry.title: What Language Models Can Inherit from Solomonoff Induction: Limits and Attainable Properties
entry.summary: What Can Language Models Inherit from Solomonoff Induction? Limits, Attainable Properties, and What Served Conditionals Reveal arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper tests the claim that scaling language models brings them closer to Solomonoff induction, using known results from algorithmic information theory, universal prediction, and Bayesian consistency. It argues that in its uniform form the claim fails for every computable model, so any closeness can only hold pointwise, one environment at a time. entry.summary: Epistemic Policy Divergence in Multi-Turn LLM Contamination: A Protocol-Gradient Investigation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies session-level contamination, where false premises inserted in earlier conversation turns are later adopted as fact by large language models. entry.summary: Have I Seen Enough? entry.summary: Opera: A Verbal Critic Framework for Long-horizon Coding Agents arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces Opera, a verbal critic framework that helps long-horizon coding agents receive corrective feedback. entry.summary: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 LLM agents often lack operational knowledge of new environments and repeat the same mistakes without memory of past attempts. entry.summary: PHASE: A Physiology-Guided Hierarchical Foundation Model for Intracranial EEG arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper introduces PHASE, a foundation model for intracranial EEG that makes directly measurable physiological characteristics explicit learning targets. entry.title: Evanescent-wave Johnson noise from superconductors, explained
entry.summary: Evanescent-wave Johnson Noise from Superconductors arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper calculates evanescent-wave Johnson noise above a superconductor's surface and the resulting relaxation time T1 of spin and charge qubits placed nanometers away. It uses a microscopic current-response kernel for a BCS superconductor, together with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and nonlocal surface impedances. entry.title: Near-optimal quantum simulation of open-system lattice dynamics, explained
entry.summary: Near-optimal quantum simulation of lattice Lindbladian dynamics arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how to simulate time evolution under geometrically local Lindbladians on a lattice of qudits. The authors present an algorithm that approximates this evolution for time t on N qudits, with diamond-norm error ε, using geometrically local circuits of depth O(t polylog(Nt/ε)). The authors state that this performance is comparable to the HHKL algorithm for lattice Hamiltonian simulation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend HHKL lattice Hamiltonian simulation to geometrically local Lindbladians, reporting local circuits of depth O(t polylog(Nt/ε)) comparable to HHKL.

entry.title: Near-optimal parallel quantum gate learning with low diamond-distance error
entry.summary: Near-Optimal Parallel Unitary Process Tomography in Diamond Distance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how to learn an unknown quantum gate (unitary process tomography), a key step toward working quantum computers. Sequential circuits were already known to achieve optimal query complexity under diamond-distance error, but it was unclear whether parallel circuits could match this. The authors introduce a new explicit parallel procedure and prove that near-optimal query complexity is achievable with parallel circuits. The gap between parallel and sequential approaches is thus closed up to a logarithmic factor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce an explicit parallel procedure that reaches near-optimal query complexity in diamond distance, narrowing the gap to sequential circuits to a logarithmic factor.

entry.title: Is rapid mixing stable? A study of whether fast relaxation in open quantum systems survives local perturbations
entry.summary: Is rapid mixing stable? arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Many open quantum systems governed by Lindbladians relax to steady states quickly, in polylogarithmic time in system size. The paper questions whether local perturbations leave this fast mixing intact. It gives counterexamples showing rapid mixing is not stable in general, even when the steady state is unchanged, and shows arbitrarily weak local Hamiltonian perturbations can destroy it. It also provides sufficient conditions guaranteeing stable rapid mixing for several classes of systems. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show rapid mixing is generally unstable via counterexamples and give several sufficient conditions for stable rapid mixing, including quasifree fermionic, commuting, and local spin systems

entry.title: Fast Hamiltonian engineering via cut polytope geometry
entry.summary: Fast Hamiltonian engineering from cut polytope geometry arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents a unified framework for Hamiltonian engineering, which simulates a target Hamiltonian's quantum dynamics using a native entangling system and restricted controls, across 2-local qubit, qudit, and fermionic systems. The authors recast time-optimal engineering as a k-cut polytope problem, prove it NP-complete, and relax it to an elliptope with Krivine-type rounding to generate pulses for a linear program. On Ising, chiral clock, and fermionic Harper-Hofstadter benchmarks, the method achieves near-optimal run times and outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, with an O(√m) approximation ratio. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce time-optimal Hamiltonian engineering to a complex k-cut polytope problem, report NP-completeness, and obtain an O(√m) approximation via elliptope relaxation with Krivine rounding, r

entry.title: Digital quantum algorithms for creating and using spin squeezed states
entry.summary: Digital Quantum Algorithms for Generating and Utilizing Spin Squeezed States arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents algorithms for efficiently generating and using spin squeezed states on digital quantum computers. The authors introduce an adaptive local-circuit protocol that prepares states with squeezing parameter ξ in depth O(log 1/ξ), which they prove is optimal for permutation symmetric states. entry.summary: Chern-number estimation: nearly optimal quantum algorithm and provable quantum speedup arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents a quantum algorithm for estimating the Chern number, a topological invariant, of a smooth Hamiltonian family over a two-dimensional parameter torus with a unique gapped ground state, including interacting many-body systems. entry.title: Proving that deciding whether the multiparameter quantum Fisher information is attainable is NP-hard
entry.summary: Deciding the Attainability of the Multiparameter Quantum Fisher Information is NP-Hard arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The quantum Fisher information sets a bound on the precision of estimating several parameters at once, but a general condition for reaching this bound with measurements on single copies of a state has been missing. This paper proves that deciding exact attainability is NP-hard, even for a restricted class of real, constant-rank quantum models. The proof reduces from deciding whether a bipartite density matrix is separable. Unless P=NP, no efficiently computable necessary and sufficient criterion exists in general. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report reducing multiparameter QFI attainability to separability and proving it NP-hard, presented as a resolution of a long-open question and a fundamental computational obstruction.

entry.summary: One-dimensional quantum Gibbs states in constant circuit depth arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper proves that the Gibbs state of any spin chain at any constant temperature is exactly a mixture of product states over bounded-length blocks of qubits. This implies such states can be prepared by constant-depth local unitary circuits with efficient classical preprocessing. entry.title: An Optimal Quantum Linear Systems Algorithm: Tight Query Bounds for Solving Linear Equations on Quantum Computers
entry.summary: An Optimal Quantum Linear Systems Algorithm arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper studies the quantum linear systems problem, where one has query access to a sparse matrix A with condition number κ and must produce a quantum state approximating the solution x of Ax = b. The authors show the query complexity is Θ(κ√d·log(1/ε)), improving previous upper and lower bounds. They also resolve an open question of Berry and Childs by showing any N×N unitary can be implemented with bounded error using O(√N) matrix-entry queries. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a tight Θ(κ√d log(1/ε)) query bound for quantum linear systems, improving prior bounds and resolving an open problem of Berry and Childs.

entry.summary: The power of oracle access: Optimal sample and query complexity of the abelian state hidden subgroup problem arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies the state hidden subgroup problem, which asks for the symmetries of an unknown quantum state. entry.title: Exponential lower bounds for low-degree strategies in quantum position-based cryptography
entry.summary: Exponential lower bounds for low-degree strategies in position-based quantum cryptography arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies lower bounds on the resources needed for non-local quantum computation (NLQC), in which two distant players cooperatively implement a bipartite unitary. The authors consider a family of diagonal ±1 unitaries indexed by Boolean hypercube elements and show that, under a low-degree polynomial condition on the first round, implementing at least one of them requires resources growing exponentially. The result matters for the security of position-based quantum cryptography, and the proof relies on type constants of particular Banach spaces and random estimates of Boolean functions. ★★★★ Notable: Addressing the open problem of exponential NLQC lower bounds, the authors report resource scaling of exp(Ω(n^{2δ}/(log n)^2)) for low-degree strategies, proved via Banach space type constants.

entry.summary: How fast can a parent estimate the value of their children? A quantum algorithm for stochastic games arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents a quantum algorithm for two-player stochastic games whose trees alternate adversarial and chance layers. It estimates the game's value using queries to leaf values and gives an upper bound on the query complexity. The authors show that quadratic speedups known for adversarial trees and single expectations both carry over when nested. ★★★★ Notable: Gives a depth-exponential bound nesting quantum adversarial search with mean estimation; the authors report both quadratic speedups survive the composition.

entry.title: Generalized LIMDDs: Compact, Canonical Decision Diagrams Modulo a Group
entry.summary: Generalized LIMDDs: Succinctness and Canonicity for Decision Diagrams Modulo a Group arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies decision diagrams for functions from {0,1}^n to C, where residual nodes are merged when they lie in one orbit of a group and the group element is recorded on edges. The group family is generated by phase rotations of order q with up to k control qubits, with or without bit flip X. The authors show exponential succinctness gains over Pauli-LIMDD, and give a five-rule reduction system with unique normal forms computable in polynomial time. ★★★★ Notable: Generalizes Myhill-Nerode quotients to group actions, reporting exponential succinctness gains over Pauli-LIMDD and a unique normal form computable in polynomial time.

entry.title: Gauge freedom and efficient algorithms for learning open quantum system dynamics
entry.summary: Gauge freedom and efficient algorithms for Lindbladian learning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies learning a local Lindbladian, which describes open quantum system dynamics, in the presence of state-preparation-and-measurement (SPAM) noise. The authors characterize this obstruction and present SPAM-robust algorithms that learn every universally gauge-invariant component using only trusted single-qubit operations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show SPAM noise can make distinct Lindbladians indistinguishable, characterize gauge freedom, and give SPAM-robust learning algorithms using Õ(ε⁻²log(N/δ)) experiments and evolution time.

entry.summary: Weakly interacting fermionic Gibbs states are Gaussian mixtures and classically simulable arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper proves that for sufficiently weak interactions, the Gibbs state of a local fermionic Hamiltonian at any finite temperature and in any spatial dimension is a convex mixture of fermionic Gaussian states. entry.summary: Log-Euclidean Rényi Conditional Mutual Information arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces a quantum Rényi conditional mutual information that measures conditional independence between quantum systems. entry.summary: Risk-Controlled Selective LLM Answering by Pricing Label-Free Checks arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces PriceCheck, which builds decision rules from label-free checks such as re-solving a problem to decide when a large language model should answer or abstain. entry.title: Revisiting dual lattice attacks on bounded distance decoding with a heuristic-free trade-off
entry.summary: Dual lattice attacks for bounded distance decoding, revisited arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper examines the assumption that scores of short dual vectors in dual lattice attacks are mutually independent. In the Haar-random lattice model, without heuristic assumptions, the authors prove an explicit asymptotic trade-off between target radius and query time for decision bounded distance decoding with preprocessing. Using Siegel and Rogers moment identities, they analyze cosine scores over complete dual balls and bound error probabilities. The resulting trade-off matches the asymptotic prediction of the Ducas-Pulles conditional model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive an explicit asymptotic BDD preprocessing trade-off in the Haar-random lattice model without heuristics, which they state matches the Ducas-Pulles conditional prediction.

entry.title: Relevance Is Not Sufficient Evidence: Spotting Missing Facts in RAG Before Answering
entry.summary: Relevance Is Not Sufficient Evidence: Detecting Evidence Gaps Before Generation in RAG arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper examines retrieval-augmented generation, where retrieved passages may name the right entities but lack the facts needed to answer. The authors build a paired benchmark and propose RINSE, which combines question coverage, answer presence in passages, and a small language model's judgment to assess sufficiency before generation. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes RINSE, judging evidence sufficiency before generation from question and passages; reports 0.837 average across six datasets, above best baseline 0.746 and a frontier model at 0.784.

entry.summary: Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper examines whether large language models, when listing concepts in a semantic fluency task, internally represent the same explore and exploit search modes found in humans. Using interpretability methods such as the Jacobian lens, the authors show that activations predict when the model switches between categories. They also show that steering these activations changes how often switching occurs. ★★★★ Notable: Extends semantic foraging to LLM internals; the authors report that J-lens activations track category switching and that steering vectors causally bias switching rates.

entry.title: Do VGGT-Family Models Need All Their Layers? A Study of Layer Redundancy and Pruning
entry.summary: Does the VGGT Family Need All Its Layers? arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This study examines which layers of the feed-forward geometry models VGGT, π³, and VGGT-Ω are needed to preserve camera poses and dense 3D structure. The resulting models reduce aggregator parameters by up to 44% while keeping accuracy comparable to the intact models. ★★★★ Notable: Studies layer redundancy across 3,018 pruned VGGT-family configurations, reporting two redundancy regions and closed-form calibration that recovers accuracy with up to 44% fewer aggregator parameters.

entry.title: On-policy distillation that reflects on visual evidence to train visual agents
entry.summary: On-Policy Visual Evidence Distillation arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Visual agents alternate between reasoning and image operations, so early errors in acquiring, reading, or grounding visual evidence can propagate through the trajectory. entry.summary: RESCUE: Repairing Language Model Errors to Sparse Circuits via Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper introduces RESCUE, a framework that locates sparse internal circuits linked to language model errors and fine-tunes only those parameters to repair the failures. It uses reinforcement learning with multiple masked-model rollouts to refine the circuit masks so they better match failures that occur during generation. entry.title: Spotter: Embodied Model Leads, Vision-Language Model Reflects and Corrects Errors
entry.summary: Spotter: Let the Embodied Model Lead, and the VLM Reflect for It arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper finds that current embodied robot models rarely repair their own failures on retry. entry.summary: MyoCodec: A Streaming Neural Codec for Electromyography arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents MyoCodec, a streaming neural codec for electromyography (EMG), the recording of muscle electrical activity. entry.title: HiTS-CL: A continual learning method for predicting future facts in evolving knowledge graphs over long time spans
entry.summary: HiTS-CL: A Continual Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Temporal Knowledge Graph Extrapolation arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Existing temporal knowledge graph reasoning methods train once on an early part of the timeline and then use a frozen model for future timestamps, which degrades over long horizons as the data changes. This paper frames extrapolative reasoning as continual learning over streaming snapshots and proposes HiTS-CL, a backbone-agnostic framework that uses continual fine-tuning for current dynamics, multi-teacher adaptive distillation for stable knowledge, and a selective memory of recent and frequent facts. HiTS-CL was integrated into five representative backbones and tested on four benchmark datasets. entry.summary: MAADBench: The Refreshable Paradigm for Anomaly Detection in Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper introduces MAADBench, the first refreshable benchmark for detecting anomalies in multi-agent systems built on large language models. entry.title: Large-scale factor analysis finds machine intelligence is only partly interpretable
entry.summary: Large-scale factor analysis shows machine intelligence is only partially interpretable arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper applies factor analysis, a psychometric method, to 13,251 evaluation scores from 1,618 language models across 456 text-only benchmarks to test whether a general intelligence factor exists. At the most generous estimate, a general factor accounts for 70.8% of performance variance, and much less in most solutions. Content-similar benchmarks do not necessarily cluster, and the factor is not dominated by a common theme or well proxied by standard intelligence benchmarks. The authors conclude this does not support treating general intelligence as a tangible target for language model development. ★★★★ Notable: A large-scale factor analysis of 1,618 language models across 456 benchmarks tests for a general intelligence factor; the authors report it explains at most 70.8% of variance and that similar-content

entry.title: LLMs Learn to Evade Latent Monitors from Prior Feedback Alone: language models learning to hide internal activity from detectors using feedback.
entry.summary: LLMs Learn to Evade Latent Monitors from Prior Feedback Alone arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper studies whether latent-space monitors, which inspect LLM internal activations to detect undesired behavior, can be evaded by agents. Models inferred the monitor's decision rule from prior verdicts and edited activations accordingly. Scaling edits by 8x cut the monitor's true positive rate from 100% to 27%, and a rank-1 LoRA reduced it to 4% on held-out concept monitors while retaining benchmark capabilities. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show models can infer latent monitor rules from feedback alone and edit activations to evade detection, reporting TPR falling to 27% with scaling and 4% with rank-1 LoRA.

entry.summary: Optimal Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies a finite-horizon Markov decision process with unknown transitions and several known reward functions, aiming to learn an ε-optimal policy for each reward using only online episodic interaction. The authors design a provably efficient algorithm with a minimax sample complexity of O(SAH³/ε² · log M) up to polylogarithmic factors, with no extra burn-in cost. entry.title: Degree balance sets a fine-grained complexity boundary for quantum SAT
entry.summary: Degree Balance as a Fine-Grained Complexity Boundary for Quantum SAT arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies the local Hamiltonian problem, a QMA-complete problem, under fine-grained complexity. Assuming the Hamiltonian is frustration-free on YES instances and approximately regular, the authors give classical and quantum algorithms that are exponentially faster than brute force. Assuming (Q)SETH, they show quantum 5-SAT has no non-trivial worst-case speedup, even when only O(√n) qubits have high degree. Reducing that high-degree set or its degrees by a factor of n^δ yields an O(2^{(1-ε)n}) algorithm. ★★★★ Notable: Under frustration-freeness and approximate regularity, the authors give exponential speedups and report a (Q)SETH lower bound nearly matching this boundary, forming a fine-grained dichotomy.

entry.title: DARE: A Dual-Path Autoregressive-Aware Method for Reducing Hallucination in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: DARE to Mitigate Hallucination: Dual-path Auto-Regressive-aware Editing arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Large vision-language models often describe objects that do not match the image, a problem called object hallucination. This paper proposes DARE, a training-free representation editing framework that reduces such hallucinations. It builds editing directions from textual contrasts, representation changes during autoregressive decoding, and controlled visual differences between paired images. entry.title: RA-CFGCache: Risk-aligned caching for faster diffusion sampling under classifier-free guidance
entry.summary: RA-CFGCache: From Branch-Level Criteria to Guided-Risk Control under Classifier-Free Guidance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper addresses the high computational cost of diffusion models under classifier-free guidance, which requires both conditional and unconditional evaluations. It proposes RA-CFGCache, a training-free caching framework that accounts for how cache errors combine across branches and how local errors affect the final output at different timesteps. An online threshold controller decides when to refresh or reuse both branches. Experiments on FLUX.1-dev, Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, and CogVideoX-2B report improved efficiency-fidelity trade-offs over evaluated training-free caching baselines. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes risk-aligned cache control for CFG that handles how branch cache errors combine and how they propagate across timesteps.
