entry.title: Longer Records, Broader Invariance: Scaling Pitfalls in Longitudinal Contrastive Learning
entry.summary: Longer Records, Broader Invariance: The Hidden Scaling Problem in Longitudinal Contrastive Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how contrastive learning on longitudinal data, which treats observations from the same person as positives, can erase meaningful behavioral change as records grow longer. The authors separate record span from supervision span and find, using in-home sensing records up to 2.7 years, that broader supervision suppresses recoverable changing-state information. They also report a prospective replication in 199 GLOBEM participants. ★★★★ Notable: Separates record span from supervision span; the authors report longer histories broaden invariance, reversible via same-person contrast, and reproduce the effect prospectively in 199 participants.

entry.title: Neural Succession: An Ecology-Inspired Theory of Forgetting in Continual Learning
entry.summary: Neural Succession: A Mesoscopic Theory of Invasion, Coexistence, and Stabilization in Continual Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper proposes Successional Learning Theory (SLT), which frames continual learning as an ecological process in which a current representation is a resident community and a new task is an invader that can displace it. Its key measure, directional pre-invasion compatibility, is computed on the resident model before the new task is learned and is strongly negatively correlated with later forgetting (r=-0.789 across 20 Split-CIFAR-10 transitions). The authors position SLT as a pre-adaptation diagnostic that complements replay, regularization, and projection methods. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a mesoscopic succession-based theory of continual learning in which pre-invasion compatibility predicts forgetting, with the authors reporting results across eight experiments.

entry.title: Audience-bound persistent memory: authorization across the whole memory lifecycle
entry.summary: Audience-Bound Persistent Memory: Authorization Across the Memory Lifecycle arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how a personal language agent acting for its owner across private and shared conversations should authorize memory before assembling context. Each memory item records the audience present when it was made, and a memory enters a model's context only if every current viewer belongs to an authorized audience. The approach was implemented in two independent architectures and an agent-memory runtime. In a pre-registered test over 10,000 multi-party histories, no forbidden item entered any architecture's context, while unscoped retrieval exposed forbidden items in 82% of contexts. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes audience-bound memory admission across the lifecycle; over 10,000 multi-party histories, no forbidden item entered context while unscoped retrieval exposed them in 82%.

entry.title: Algorithm for Arctic product-mix auction equilibria
entry.summary: Solving the Arctic Product-Mix Auction arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies Arctic product-mix auctions, where budget-constrained bidders express preferences over multiple substitute goods. It gives the first strongly polynomial algorithm for finding competitive equilibria when the auctioneer has separable convex piecewise-linear costs. The method combines a strongly polynomial reduction to the costless Arctic auction with an existing strongly polynomial algorithm for that case. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first strongly polynomial algorithm for competitive equilibria of Arctic auctions with separable convex costs, plus reductions to linear Fisher and Arrow-Debreu markets.

entry.title: Training LLMs to Say When They Know They're Being Evaluated
entry.summary: Training LLMs to Verbalize Evaluation Awareness arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Language models may act differently during audits when they are aware they are being evaluated, which makes such behavior hard to measure. This paper introduces verbalization training (VT), which uses spontaneous statements of evaluation awareness as evidence and trains models with reinforcement learning to verbalize it more readily. Across three models, VT raised verbalized evaluation awareness 2.4 to 2.9 times and transferred to held-out agentic settings, while latent awareness and behavior stayed largely stable. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes verbalization training, which the authors report raises verbalized evaluation awareness 2.4–2.9x across three models, with a synthetic-document fine-tuning causal experiment.

entry.summary: MoRE: Scaling mixture of experts with hardware-aware low-rank routing arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper proposes MoRE, which factorizes the router weight matrix of Mixture-of-Experts layers into low rank, reducing routing cost to O((h+M)r). entry.title: CyFA: Linear sequence model that stores past associations in relative-time slots
entry.summary: CyFA: Linear Sequence Modeling with Relative-Time-Partitioned Memory arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper introduces CyFA (Cyclic Flow Attention), a linear RNN whose memory is partitioned by relative time. A learned clock cyclically transports key and value states so stored associations are organized across relative-time slots. Pretraining experiments at 400M to 1.4B parameters report better recall-intensive performance, competitive language modeling, and high computational efficiency. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes relative-time-partitioned memory organized by cyclic transport; the authors derive an exact absolute-clock reformulation enabling chunk-wise training, and report 400M–1.4B pretraining results

entry.summary: Action Chunking Proximal Policy Optimization with Feedback Correction arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper proposes ACPPO, a PPO extension whose actor outputs action chunks while keeping a standard state-value critic, avoiding chunked Q-functions. entry.summary: ChronoSRL: Temporal Geometry for Self-Supervised Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper introduces ChronoSRL, a reinforcement learning method that trains the critic's embedding distances to match the time an agent needs to reach a goal. entry.title: Influence maximization in near-linear time: a faster method for choosing key seed nodes
entry.summary: Maximizing Social Influence in Almost Linear Time arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies influence maximization, which seeks k seed nodes in a graph with n nodes and m edges to maximize expected information spread under standard diffusion models. The prior Borgs et al. algorithm ran in Õ((n+m)k) time, and later work only reduced log factors or improved the dependence on ε. The authors present an algorithm achieving a 1−1/e−ε approximation in Õ(n+m) time, removing the multiplicative dependence on k from the running time. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present an algorithm achieving a 1-1/e-ε approximation for influence maximization in near-linear time, removing the multiplicative dependence on k and answering a long-open question.

entry.title: Training neural operators from equations alone, using a preconditioned loss
entry.summary: Preconditioned Physics-Informed Neural Operator Training arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Neural operators are usually trained with data from a classical solver, which is costly to generate. This paper proposes a preconditioned residual loss that fixes the ill-conditioning of physics-informed losses, so the model can be trained purely from governing equations. entry.title: From Classical to Quantum Channels: Positive Covert Communication Rates
entry.summary: From Classical to Quantum Channels: Achieving Positive Covert Rates arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper examines when covert communication at positive rates is possible over discrete memoryless classical, classical-quantum, and quantum channels. For classical point-to-point channels, positive covert rates are achievable for certain channel classes when the input alphabet is larger than the output alphabet. For quantum channels, if the innocent state is mixed, a non-trivial input ensemble can always satisfy the covertness constraint. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give new conditions for positive covert rates over classical, cq, and quantum channels, extending to MACs; they report that input dimension exceeding output dimension yields achievability.

entry.title: Reasoning with Neural Cellular Automata: Testing visual reasoning using only local connections
entry.summary: Reasoning with Neural Cellular Automata arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper tests whether Neural Cellular Automata, networks using only local connectivity and asynchronous updates, can perform complex multi-step reasoning. entry.title: Rendering Inputs as Images to Defend Against Prompt Injection
entry.summary: Render Before Reading: Visual Rendering as a Prompt Injection Defense arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper finds that multimodal LLMs are more likely to follow adversarial instructions delivered as text than when the same instructions arrive as images. Building on this modality gap, the authors propose Pictionary, a training-free defense that renders untrusted content as typographic images or audio before it reaches the model. Across ten models and two benchmarks, the method consistently reduces attack success rates while largely preserving benign utility, including against adaptive attacks and human red teamers. ★★★★★ Notable: Finds multimodal LLMs follow text-form injected instructions more than image-form ones, and proposes a training-free rendering defense that the authors report reduces attack success across ten models

Easy questions decline sharply while difficult questions become more common, with rising code complexity. Data-rich topics lose share while data-scarce ones gain, and the easy-question decline is concentrated in data-rich domains. entry.title: Mnemon: a long-term memory agent for LLM assistants that splits work into fast judgments and slow reasoning
entry.summary: Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper introduces Mnemon, a memory agent for LLM assistants that keeps conversations as raw dated records instead of rewriting them at write time. An LLM plans searches, a fast decision model called Jev judges the returned records, and explicit budget rules assemble a small context for the answering model. The authors report top scores on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with small per-question context and slow cost growth on the BEAM benchmark. ★★★★ Notable: Splits memory work into fast batch judgments over raw dated records and slow LLM planning; the authors report 91.7% on LoCoMo and 83.8% on LongMemEval-S.

entry.title: Proof that the best known bound for preferent compression is tight
entry.summary: Preferent Compression Bounds Are Tight arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper concerns sample compression, a method for producing safety and performance guarantees for learning-based systems. Sharp bounds exist for algorithms with a preference (stability) property, but whether they are tight was an open question. The authors show the current best bound is tight, using an explicit construction based on the uniform distribution and order statistics. They also give a shorter proof relying only on elementary counting. ★★★★ Notable: Addresses whether preferent compression bounds are tight, reporting an explicit uniform-distribution construction that attains the bound in the limit, plus a shorter elementary proof.

entry.title: Same Text, Different Authority: How Reserved Tokens Make Chat-Template Prompt Injection Stronger
entry.summary: Same Bytes, Different Authority: Reserved-Token Representations in Chat-Template Prompt Injection arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies prompt injection against LLM agents, finding that forged chat-template markers such as <|im_start|> are far more effective when fed to the model as reserved control tokens than as ordinary subwords. Encoding the same text as subwords lowered attack success on the InjecAgent benchmark by 39 to 66 percentage points on three of four open-weight families. The standard tokenizer mitigation covers only tokens a configuration declares special, so tool-protocol tokens remain unprotected and the gap persists on that channel. ★★★★★ Notable: Shows that the same text encoded as a reserved control token versus subwords changes forged-marker injection authority, quantified on InjecAgent and AgentDojo, with implications for defense.

entry.title: MMSkillRisk: Can AI agents stay safe when image-based skills hide malicious instructions?
entry.summary: MMSkillRisk: Can Agents Stay Safe When Multimodal Skills Become Traps? arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces MMSkillRisk, a benchmark for end-to-end safety testing of attacks hidden in images within multimodal agent skills. The authors design NCVA, an attack that disguises malicious instructions as native parts of teaching images, such as annotations and interface labels. Across nine model-harness configurations, NCVA reaches a pooled attack success rate of 43.1%, 16.4 percentage points above a text-carrier baseline. The results show attacks can succeed while legitimate tasks are also completed, so task success alone does not prove safe skill use. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report that NCVA, an image-borne attack, reaches 43.1% pooled ASR in isolated sandboxes, 16.4 points above the text-carrier baseline across nine configurations.

entry.title: TokenCast: Predicting Token Use During LLM Agent Runs
entry.summary: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Token consumption by a large language model agent can vary widely across runs of the same task, and growing context raises the input cost of each later call. TokenCast learns a composable cost representation for each execution segment and combines adjacent segments to estimate cumulative consumption, refreshing the forecast as the run proceeds without extra LLM calls. entry.title: λ-JEPA: Spectral Anti-Collapse Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning
entry.summary: λ-JEPA Spectral Anti-Collapse Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies representation collapse in joint-embedding self-supervised learning, finding that anti-collapse objectives applied after a projection head may not prevent dimensional collapse in the backbone. The authors propose SACReg, a spectral regularizer motivated by λ-balance analysis, and apply it to JEPA as λ-JEPA. According to the paper, λ-JEPA outperforms LeJEPA and VISReg on ImageNet-1k classification and average linear-probe transfer across eight image datasets, and improves over LeVJEPA and V-JEPA 2 on video benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: Introduces SACReg, a lambda-balance spectral anti-collapse regularizer for JEPA, with linear-network analysis and reported comparisons to LeJEPA and V-JEPA 2 on ImageNet and video benchmarks.

entry.title: CAR-VLA: Complexity- and Risk-Aware Reasoning for Self-Driving
entry.summary: CAR-VLA: Complexity-Aware and Risk-Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper proposes CAR-VLA, a driving vision-language-action model that uses both scene complexity and dynamic risk to decide how reasoning should be performed. entry.summary: Coherence-Aware Distributional Evaluation of Open-Ended Text Generation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper argues that existing open-ended generation metrics can miss global coherence failures, such as passages that are locally fluent but globally contradictory. entry.summary: Frozen Judges, Moving Agents: Version-Dependent LLM-Judge Error and the Limits of Judge-Assisted Agent Evaluation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies whether language-model judges can fairly compare new and old versions of AI agents, finding that a fixed judge can make version-dependent errors. entry.summary: PDMD: Projected Distribution Matching Distillation for Video Diffusion Models arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper proposes PDMD, a modification of Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) that reduces the number of denoising steps needed by video diffusion models while keeping output quality stable. The authors attribute training degradation, such as oversaturation and artifacts, to critic errors and filter them by projecting out a component of the DMD update. entry.summary: Denoising Multi-Robot Trajectories arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper builds on D4orm, a dynamics-aware diffusion-denoising framework, to plan trajectories for multiple robots. entry.title: Learning sparse quantum states using only single-qubit measurements

entry.summary: Share-Borne AI Virus: Memory-Hopping Attacks Across LLM Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how large language model assistants that share persistent artifacts, such as reports, can unintentionally pass adversarial content between one another. Malicious content is stored in an assistant's memory, reproduced in later artifacts, and picked up by other assistants. The authors simulate artifact exchange among independent assistants to measure survival across hand-offs, hop count, and spread. entry.summary: Universal Approximation of Measure-to-Measure Operators by Pushforwards arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies whether continuous operators between spaces of probability measures can be approximated by pushforward models whose transformation depends on the input distribution. entry.summary: Manifold-Stable Flow Matching arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper introduces manifold-stable flow matching (MSFM), which can start from an arbitrary ambient prior, not necessarily supported on the data manifold. It uses contraction theory to combine learned tangential transport with prescribed normal contraction, using analytical projectors for known manifolds and PCA-estimated local affine proxies for unknown ones. entry.title: SOLO: Training Billion-Parameter Language Models Locally with a Shared Output Readout
entry.summary: SOLO: Pretraining Billion-Parameter Language Models with Shared-Output Local Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper proposes SOLO (Shared-Output LOcal learning), which replaces each module's private readout with a shared, read-only copy of the final module's readout, so that every module receives information from the whole network without passing gradients between modules. On Transformers with 340M to 2B parameters pretrained on 15B tokens, SOLO stays within one point of backpropagation in average zero-shot accuracy. entry.summary: Convex Optimization Is Free When Accuracy Is Expensive arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper studies convex optimization when gradients can only be approximated, with computational cost growing as δ^(-γ) in accuracy δ. entry.title: Lasting Partners Push Up Prices Among Learning Pricing Agents
entry.summary: Persistent Partners Raise Prices Among Learning Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies pricing agents that repeatedly meet on a platform, asking whether the platform's choice of who faces whom changes the prices the agents learn. Using the Bertrand duopoly model of Calvano et al., prices are set by tabular Q-learning, with randomized assignment of keeping the same partner, seeing rival prices, and messaging. Keeping the same partner raised average training-period profit levels by 0.27 of the gap between competitive and monopoly profit (95% CI 0.20 to 0.35). ★★★★ Notable: A preregistered experiment reports fixed partners lift learned-agent profit levels by 0.27 and separates learned punishment from static best response, for algorithmic collusion research.

entry.title: First learn, then memorize: why diffusion models generalize before they memorize
entry.summary: First Learn, Then Memorize: The Spectral Bias of Diffusion Models arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies why diffusion models trained on a finite dataset first generate novel samples and only later collapse onto their training set. The authors show that training dynamics are governed by the Neural Tangent Kernel Gram matrix on noisy data, and that repeated noising splits its spectrum into a large-eigenvalue part linked to generalization and a small-eigenvalue part linked to memorization. Analytical results in high-dimensional limits and experiments on CelebA and U-Nets support this picture, and truncating the Gram matrix or penalizing the second bulk is shown to tune the transition. ★★★★ Notable: The authors explain diffusion models' generalize-then-memorize timescales via two spectral bulks of the NTK Gram matrix, reporting analysis plus CelebA and U-Net experiments and causal interventions.

entry.summary: Weighting Schedules Govern What and When Score-Based Generative Models Learn from Multimodal Data arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies how score-based generative models learn multimodal distributions during training. At high signal-to-noise ratio, all mode directions are learned together on one timescale while relative weights are not learned. entry.summary: Narrow Multimodal Fine-Tuning Can Induce Emergent Misalignment arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies whether fine-tuning vision-language models on narrow multimodal tasks, such as vulnerable code, careless household-object use, and conspiratorial readings of ordinary scenes, can cause emergent misalignment. Across fifteen commercial and open-source models, the authors find that such fine-tuning induces broadly misaligned behavior that transfers to unrelated tasks. They also test mitigation strategies that partially reduce this effect. ★★★★★ Notable: First extension of narrow-task fine-tuning induced emergent misalignment to vision-language models; the authors report it transfers to unrelated tasks across fifteen commercial and open-source models

entry.title: AIM-ZO: Activation-guided subspace maintenance for memory-efficient LLM fine-tuning without backpropagation
entry.summary: AIM-ZO: Activation-Informed Subspace Maintenance for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper proposes AIM-ZO, a zeroth-order method for fine-tuning large language models that estimates updates using only forward evaluations, avoiding backpropagation and activation storage. entry.title: Envy-free splits of random assignments, with four agents solved
entry.summary: Envy-Free Decompositions of Random Assignments: Settling Four Agents, and What Lies Beyond arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies whether a random assignment of objects to agents can be decomposed into deterministic assignments so that every agent envies any other with probability at most 1/2. It proves this is always possible for four agents using a computer-aided check over all vertices, and shows 1/2 is the best general threshold. It also gives proofs for special cases and shows some natural decomposition methods fail. Deciding whether an arbitrary random assignment admits such a decomposition is strongly NP-complete. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that every four-agent SD-EF random assignment admits a Dec-EF decomposition via a computer-aided proof, and prove strong NP-completeness for the general decision problem.

entry.title: Subgroup rank-1 lattice points for fast high-dimensional black-box integral estimation
entry.summary: Subgroup Rank-1 Lattice for Practical High-dimensional Black-box Integral Approximation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper proposes subgroup rank-1 lattice point sets for estimating integrals of high-dimensional black-box functions, such as kernel mean embeddings and the softmax kernel in self-attention. Restricting the Korobov generator to a fixed multiplicative order allows feature-map computations to be done exactly by FFT in O(n log m) time and O(n) memory. The authors prove a convergence rate for the squared worst-case error and report better results than random features and scrambled Sobol' and Halton points across synthetic and real-data settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine subgroup rank-1 lattices with FFT to cut feature-map integration to O(n log m) time and O(n) memory, and report a worst-case error decay of O(n^{-(α-1)/(m-1)}) in the Korobov space

entry.title: AReaL-TIK: An agent that optimizes unified RL GPU kernels using a search-tracking representation
entry.summary: AReaL-TIK: Stateful Agentic Optimization of Unified RL Kernels through an Optimization IR arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Reinforcement learning post-training often uses separate GPU kernels for rollout and policy updates, and numerical differences can distort probability ratios. The paper introduces KernelBraid, an agentic framework that starts from a hand-tuned, bitwise-consistent unified kernel and organizes code search with an optimization intermediate representation. Changes are kept only if they pass correctness checks and improve aggregate latency. Across 12 end-to-end training setups on H20, it reaches 1.10x average throughput relative to AReaL with log-probability recomputation. ★★★★ Notable: KernelBraid uses an optimization IR to guide agentic search for bitwise-consistent RL kernels; the authors report 1.10x average throughput over AReaL across 12 end-to-end configurations.

entry.summary: UniOPSD: Unifying Outcome and Hindsight Feedback for Agentic Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces UniOPSD, a method for training language model agents that merges environment rewards with hindsight feedback from successful peer responses. entry.title: Automatic self-reduction gives stronger randomized distributed lower bounds
entry.summary: Distributed Lower Bounds via Automatic Self-Reduction arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies randomized lower bounds for graph problems in the distributed setting. The authors show that self-reduction is a special case of classical round elimination and introduce a new error measure under which round elimination yields bounds beyond ω(log log n). They identify a class of problems where this improvement applies black-box. The paper proves Ω(√log n) randomized lower bounds for maximal matching on regular 2-colored graphs, 1/k-integral matching, and maximal H-packing. ★★★★★ Notable: Recasts self-reduction as a special case of classical round elimination via a new error measure, yielding ω(log log n) randomized lower bounds and Ω(√log n) bounds for several graph problems.

entry.summary: Optimizing and Securing the Modern Watermarking Channel for Images arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Recent rules require traceable generated content, so modern watermarking uses post-hoc multi-bit schemes built from neural encoder-decoder pairs. The paper analyzes these networks statistically and shows they implicitly form parallel AWGN channels with BPSK modulation, which limits capacity and lacks a secret key, making them insecure. entry.summary: SeLMRoute: Probabilistic Semantic Evidence for Large Language Model Routing arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces SeLMRoute, a framework that selects the most suitable large language model for each query. entry.summary: Depth-Optimal Quantum Compilation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper presents the first constant-depth circuit for synthesizing arbitrary single-qubit gates, a construction that is fully unitary and needs no pre-supplied catalyst. entry.summary: A General Harness for Protein Foundation Model Fitness Prediction arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper introduces VenusREM-Harness (VRH), a model-agnostic, training-free retrieval-enhanced mutation harness that improves protein foundation models' fitness predictions. It fuses frozen model scores with multiple sequence alignment evidence weighted by model uncertainty, then applies background correction and shrinkage based on structural confidence and solvent exposure. entry.summary: Backdoor as Probe: Test-Time Adversarial Defense for CLIP arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper proposes Backdoor as Probe (BaP), a test-time adversarial defense for the CLIP vision-language model that requires no retraining. entry.title: ActionLens: A Benchmark for Diagnosing Who-Does-What-When Errors in Video AI Models
entry.summary: ActionLens: Diagnosing Spatial-Temporal Binding Failures in Vision-Language Models arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper introduces ActionLens, a diagnostic benchmark of 6,701 multiple-choice video questions testing whether vision-language models can link the right action to the right person at the right moment. Answers are derived from 1.58 million per-second, per-person annotations across five diagnostics, including gaze detection. Across 20 models, the best scores 65.9% on the human-reviewed subset versus 91.0% for humans, with gaze detection near chance. entry.summary: Near-Optimal Bounds on the Density of Low-Energy States of k-Local Hamiltonians and Faster Quantum Algorithms arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies low-energy estimation and state preparation for general k-local Hamiltonians, two basic problems in quantum complexity theory. entry.summary: SEAD: A State-Based Perspective on Attack and Defense in Tool-Using Agents arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper frames attacks and defenses on language-model agents that use tools as partially observed state control, since earlier actions can change state so that a later routine-looking action becomes harmful. entry.summary: Nash Equilibria in Auctions with Pacing Strategies: Complexity and Inefficiency arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies Auctions with Pacing Strategies (APS) games, where utility-maximizing bidders across many simultaneous first-price auctions each choose one pacing multiplier that scales their bids. entry.summary: On the Relation Between Interval Regret and Dynamic Regret arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies two performance metrics for online learning in changing environments: interval regret and dynamic regret. It shows that an algorithm with optimal interval regret can still fail to achieve optimal dynamic regret, for both convex and curved functions. The authors then propose a reduction that invokes interval regret minimization over an enlarged Euclidean ball with a domain-converted surrogate loss, achieving optimal dynamic regret. entry.summary: Quantum Security of XOR of Permutations via Fourier Analysis arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies whether the XOR of several independent random permutations (XoP) stays secure against quantum attacks that query it in superposition. The authors prove explicit upper bounds on the advantage of any q-query quantum algorithm in distinguishing XoP from a random function. The bounds hold across the whole query range well beyond the 2^(n/3) limit from quantum collision finding. entry.title: Commutator Memory: a readout of training-order path dependence in language models
entry.summary: Commutator Memory: Sparse, Path-Local Reading and Steering in Language Models arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies how training a language model on two data sources in opposite orders leaves different weights, and asks whether this difference forms a parametric memory of training history. The authors approximate the weight difference with a Lie bracket of the two gradient fields and project it onto vocabulary tokens to get one score per token. They report that these scores are localized, that downweighting top-scoring tokens closes part of the measured loss gap in Qwen-3-4B SFT, and that the trained weights can identify which order produced them in 92% of cases. ★★★★ Notable: Defines training-order memory via a Lie bracket projected onto tokens; reports localization across three models and that downweighting top tokens closes a median 32% of the gap.

entry.summary: Dynamical Parameters: An Interpretability Framework for Time-Series Foundation Models arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper examines a gap in time-series foundation models: a dynamical property can be read from a hidden state, yet the forecast may not respond correctly when that property changes.
